guidance: A quick drawing of a GeoJSON file, not a survey or cartographic product: coordinates are WGS84 longitude and latitude, properties are ignored, and there is no basemap, so check a production map against a GIS before publishing it.
method: A GeoJSON document is read as WGS84 longitude and latitude in degrees, in that order, and every position is checked before anything is drawn: the type must be a FeatureCollection, a Feature, a GeometryCollection or one of the six geometry types, features must be Feature objects, longitudes must lie within -180 to 180 and latitudes within -90 to 90, a line string needs two positions and a polygon ring three. An open ring is closed with a warning, a null geometry is skipped with a warning, and a document with no coordinates is refused. Positions are collected in document order, and each line or ring is unwrapped so that consecutive longitudes differ by at most 180 degrees; a polygon that crosses the antimeridian therefore takes longitudes past 180 instead of stretching back across the whole map, and the bounds are reported in that unwrapped frame. The drawing then uses one of two projections. Equirectangular maps longitude straight to x and latitude straight to y, so one degree of latitude looks the same length as one degree of longitude even though it is not. Web Mercator maps latitude to y = ln(tan(pi/4 + phi/2)) in radians, multiplied by 180/pi so the units match longitude degrees at the equator; it is conformal but inflates area with latitude, and it is undefined at the poles, so latitudes beyond +/-85.05112878 degrees are clamped and a warning is shown. Both projections are fitted with a single uniform scale into a four-to-three frame with a padding of 3.5 percent of the width (16 to 40 pixels), so the aspect ratio of the data is preserved and the smaller dimension is centred. Polygons become filled paths with the even-odd rule so holes work, line strings become stroked paths, and points become circles. The optional graticule takes the smallest step from 0.005, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 30 and 45 degrees that yields at most eight intervals, and labels each line at the edge. The output is one standalone SVG with its own dark background, so it opens without this site. The page does not read properties, styling, CRS members or elevation, it does not fetch tiles or a basemap, it does not repair topology, and it is not a geodetic library: it is a quick drawing of a file. Everything runs in the browser; nothing is uploaded, stored or sent anywhere.
